essential: Leaving Dixwell's school in June 1854 with 'unqualified joy.' New England boys were 'born too old'; Harvard was attended by custom, not taken seriously.
Harvard's Unitarian 'mesure': it created 'a type but not a will' and left a water-mark. It was the least hurtful university, and left the mind supple.
He got nothing from distinguished mates. Give a condensed portrait of the Class of 1858: negative, self-distrustful, formidable critics, judgment 'a sort of gravitation.'

The Virginians: Roony Lee, son of Colonel Robert E. Lee, with his Petersburg 'staff,' plus Anderson. Lee had the habit of command, was popular, then faded, being 'simple beyond analysis.' Keep the danger of drink and the knife or pistol, and Lee keeping his staff under control.

Adams liked them. He suspected two eighteenth-century types were equally unfit for an economist's America. Both failed, Lee totally and Adams partially. Lee took Winfield Scott's commission against the Mormons and asked Adams to write his acceptance letter: 'The diplomat felt his profession.'

Masters taught little. He was graded precisely in the middle, which he later checked in the class-lists when a professor himself. Mathematics was a failure. He heard nothing of Marx or Comte; chemistry befogged him. Agassiz's lectures on the Glacial Period and Paleontology alone stirred him. Four years equalled four months.
Harvard as a negative force: it weakened political bias. He turned to writing and accepted the instructors' middling ranking.
Lowell opened the door to Germany. The literary world's German faith was a revolt against coming capitalism. Reading privately in Lowell's study was the one gain.

Concord: he approached as one entering a cathedral where priests thought him a worm. He was slipping from fixed principles, but never reached Concord. The universe seemed real to him, and Lowell was 'as little transcendental as Beacon Street.' He got encouragement for two years in Europe.

Social position was his only capital; he made no useful acquaintance. Richardson the friendship of later life, though not owing to college, like La Farge, St. Gaudens, King, and Hay. 'Life is a narrow valley.' College's social habit perpetuated an inferior type. Hence 'He took to the pen. He wrote.'

Writing met silence and his own felt limits: 'when he had nothing to say, he could not say it.' He was elected Class Orator over the first scholar to his bewilderment. The class repeatedly chose those least representative of them, 'mirrors.'

Class Day: the oration forgotten; an uncle's 'wanting in enthusiasm'; 'perfect self-possession.' Harvard gave calm, the Hasty Pudding as the most terrible audience. Whether this was education he never knew. End: 'Education had not begun.'
optional: The names in the College Catalogue (Agassiz, Brooks, Holmes), keeping Richardson for later.
The full adjectival portrait of the class can be shortened.
The list of German-faith writers and the Thackeray, Dickens, Balzac satire sentence.
The sentence about the vices of drinking being less harmful than the virtues, reduced to one clause.
The Council of Trent / Sir Anthony Absolute comparison; cut together with the Hasty Pudding mention, or keep both.
risks: Several overlapping negative verdicts on Harvard. Cutting them risks flattening the progression from 'negative force' to 'self-possession,' which should stay distinct.

title: HARVARD COLLEGE (1854-1858)

verbatim.purpose: Core image of the college's effect.
verbatim.text: Four years of Harvard College, if successful, resulted in an autobiographical blank, a mind on which only a water-mark had been stamped.
It taught little, and that little ill, but it left the mind open, free from bias, ignorant of facts, but docile.

verbatim.purpose: Aphoristic deflation of the class's independence.
verbatim.text: yet to stand alone is quite natural when one has no passions; still easier when one has no pains.

verbatim.purpose: Blunt typological judgment, later qualified by Adams's own likeness to Lee.
verbatim.text: Strictly, the Southerner had no mind; he had temperament.
he needed to read mathematics, like any other universal language, and he never reached the alphabet.
remained always an insect, or something much lower--a man.

verbatim.purpose: Climactic image of the classmates as judges.
verbatim.text: like so many mirrors of himself, an infinite reflection of his own shortcomings.
As yet he knew nothing. Education had not begun.

voice_profile: Third-person autobiography in which the aged author calls his younger self 'he,' 'the boy,' or 'Henry Adams.' It moves between the child's limited view and the old man's retrospective irony. It relies on aphorism and paradox, such as 'Summer was the multiplicity of nature; winter was school.' Self-deprecation is played as mock-scientific analysis: variation, type, force, stamp. Long periodic sentences end in a dry reversal. Lists build through dashes and semicolons. Exact dates anchor the account. Qualifiers like 'perhaps,' 'probably,' and 'he could never decide' recur. Every episode is measured as a lesson in education that taught little or the wrong thing. Double hyphens are characteristic and must be kept.
